brief: Every record below has two kinds of time. Valid time is when the address was true in the world. System time is when the store recorded it, and when a later record superseded it.
Nothing here is ever overwritten. A correction appends a new record, and a mistake is marked superseded rather than deleted. Where two records cover the same moment, the one recorded later wins.
Answer each question by fixing two dates: the moment in the world you are asking about, and the moment of knowledge you are asking from. Then read off what the store believed.
subject: Customer 4812's shipping address

facts.note: The original address, captured when the customer opened the account on 5 January.
A real move, recorded promptly: the customer updated the address in the app on moving day.
An erroneous record: a support agent mistyped the street during a phone call. It was marked superseded on 16 March when a parcel came back.
The correction appended on 16 March. It restates the right address from 1 March, and the mistyped record stays in the store.
A late retroactive correction: the customer moved on 1 April but only told the company on 6 May, five weeks later.

questions.prompt: As of 30 June, what did the store believe the address was on 2 January?
questions.explanation: No record is valid before 5 January, when the account was opened. Even with everything known by 30 June, the store holds no address for that day.

questions.prompt: As of 10 March, what did the store believe the address was on 5 March?
questions.explanation: On 10 March the mistyped record, made on 2 March, had not yet been superseded. It was the latest record covering 5 March, so the store believed the wrong street.

questions.prompt: As of 20 March, what did the store believe the address was on 5 March?
questions.explanation: Same moment in the world, later knowledge. By 20 March the error was superseded and the correction appended on 16 March is the latest visible record.

questions.prompt: As of 20 April, what did the store believe the address was on 15 April?
questions.explanation: The customer had already moved to Hull, but the store did not learn that until 6 May. On 20 April its best knowledge was still Mill Street, so a parcel sent then was not a mistake.

questions.prompt: As of 10 May, what did the store believe the address was on 15 April?
questions.explanation: The late correction recorded on 6 May is valid from 1 April. Asked from 10 May, the store now says the customer lived in Hull on 15 April, even though it said otherwise on 20 April.
